 13 years, billions of dollars and a return to Vice City. Why GTA VI could break every record
 From record-breaking trailers to marathon livestreams, GTA VI has become a global obsession even before its release.
 Raunaq Lekhi 
 16 November, 2026 03:56 pm IST

 New Delhi: Thirteen years, two generations of consoles, countless memes and enough fan theories to fill an entire internet rabbit hole. The wait for Grand Theft Auto VI is almost over. And Rockstar Games isn’t just preparing to release another video game. It could be about to deliver one of the biggest entertainment launches in history. 
 GTA VI arrives on 19 November, with analysts projecting a staggering $3.25 billion to $5.2 billion in sales by the end of its first week. That would put the game in a league of its own, far beyond the opening numbers of most Hollywood blockbusters. 
 From streamers planning marathon sessions to fans dissecting every frame of its trailers, GTA VI has become a pop-culture obsession long before anyone has played it. 
 Show Full Article
 Can GTA VI really make $5 billion in a week? 
 The numbers are extraordinary, even by Rockstar’s standards. 
 According to gaming analytics firm Newzoo , GTA VI generated an estimated $260 million in global digital pre-orders during the first week they became available in June. 
 Using historical sales patterns, the firm projected between $3.25 billion and $5.2 billion in cumulative sales by the end of launch week, equivalent to roughly 37 million to 59 million copies depending on pricing assumptions. 
 Its central estimate puts sales at approximately $4.5 billion, or 51 million copies. 
 These are projections, not confirmed earnings. But the scale becomes clearer when compared with GTA V, which made $800 million in its first 24 hours and crossed $1 billion within three days of its September 2013 launch. 
 GTA VI could surpass that three-day milestone within hours. 
 What is GTA VI actually about? 
 Forget Los Santos. Rockstar is taking players back to Vice City, its neon-soaked, Miami-inspired playground, this time within the sprawling fictional state of Leonida. 
 At the centre are Jason Duval, a former soldier drawn into drug running, and Lucia Caminos, a woman recently released from prison. 
 Their story follows a couple whose criminal ambitions spiral into a much larger conspiracy. Think Bonnie and Clyde, only with Florida highways, nightclubs, swamps, luxury yachts and Rockstar’s trademark satire of American excess. 
 Unlike GTA V’s three protagonists, GTA VI focuses on two central characters whose relationship drives the story. 
 Rockstar has also introduced a colourful supporting cast, including drug dealers, aspiring musicians and social-media personalities. 
 How big is the gameplay, and how long will it take to finish? 
 Rockstar promises a bigger, more detailed open world, stretching beyond Vice City’s beaches and skyscrapers into Leonida’s wetlands, small towns and coastal communities. 
 Players can expect the familiar GTA mix of driving, shootouts, police pursuits and exploration, alongside wildlife, water activities and a more reactive environment. 
 Previews have pointed towards improved character interactions, realistic vehicle handling and greater freedom in approaching encounters. 
 But one question remains unanswered. How long will GTA VI actually take to finish? 
 Rockstar has not confirmed the main story’s length. Online estimates suggesting 60 to 80 hours remain speculative, and the total could be considerably higher for players exploring side activities. 
 Details about the game’s eventual online multiplayer experience also remain limited. 
 Why has the hype reached another level? 
 GTA V has sold more than 230 million copies worldwide, while GTA Online has kept millions returning for over a decade. 
 That enormous audience has spent 13 years waiting for a proper sequel. 
 The first GTA VI trailer crossed 90 million YouTube views in 24 hours in December 2023. Rockstar said the second trailer attracted 475 million views across platforms in its first day. 
 Every delay, leak and trailer has only intensified the anticipation. 
 The launch also arrives in an era dominated by Twitch, YouTube livestreams, TikTok clips and viral gaming moments. Millions who never buy GTA VI could still experience its opening days through streamers, memes and social media. 
 For Rockstar, the challenge is no longer simply selling millions of copies. It is delivering a game capable of living up to 13 years of expectations. 
 The world has waited long enough. On Thursday, Vice City finally opens its doors.
